utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So, good morning, everybody. Madam Registrar, could you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-05-88-T, the Prosecutor versus Vujadin Popovic et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, ma'am. All the accused are here. Amongst the Defence teams I only notice the absence of Mr. Sarapa. I suppose he is helping you in the office, Mr. Haynes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: He was in the building a short while ago. I imagine he will be here at the first break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. And from the Prosecution side I see Mr. McCloskey and Mr. Thayer. I understand there are some preliminaries. Madam Fauveau.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, could we go into private session for a moment, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Certainly. Let's go into private session please, for a while.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So basically -- I thank you, Mr. Bourgon, for responding orally on behalf of the other Defence teams to the Prosecution motion requesting additional time to comply with the Trial Chamber's 7th March order setting dead-lines for submissions regarding the admissibility of intercept evidence and also for informing us that there are negotiations ongoing or discussions ongoing with the Prosecution, the background being the express wish that you have to bring forward some expert evidence before the whole issue of admissibility of intercepts is finally decided by the Trial Chamber. We thank you also, Mr. McCloskey, for your comment. We distance ourselves -- we would not pronounce ourselves on whether this is -- would be relevant for admissibility or not. I think on the face of it, it would be. I can tell you that when we were preparing our 7th March order, the question of whether there would be the need for evidence brought forward by the Defence was something that we discussed, but since we are still in the stage of the Prosecution case, and we are never going to be in a position during that stage to force you to bring evidence during the Prosecution stage, we obviously omitted going into that area in our decision. But, of course, if there is a request on the part of the Defence teams to bring forward evidence and that evidence is on the face of it relevant for the issues to be determined by this Trial Chamber, obviously we will decide on that. All right. So, Mr. Josse now. Let's go into private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: We can start in open session, having thought about it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Josse. Give me one moment. Okay. I found the motion. Yes, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Your Honour, first of all, as I have already said, we oppose protective measures for both of these witnesses, particularly 49, if I may say. But dealing with the matter generally first of all and to some extent, as my learned friends have already said, as a matter of principle, we submit that the reasons contained within in particular motion are wholly inadequate. They don't contain remotely enough detail to satisfy the Chamber. On the basis of the concerns, as detailed in this motion, virtually any witness would have protective measures. Indeed, any witness would have some concerns at giving evidence at this court. Perhaps not any witness, but many, many witnesses would, particularly bearing in mind the subject matter of the things they have to testify about. We submit the burden is heavily on the party calling the witness to satisfy the Chamber that there are real reasons for the concerns and that there are concrete examples as to why those concerns might, in some way, come to -- if I can put it like this, fruition in the future, in other words, something will happen so as to mean it necessitates the Court actually imposing protective measures in relation to these particular witnesses. Perhaps if I go through the witnesses in turn briefly, we should go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, let's do that. Please.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: The information --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: I beg your pardon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good morning to you, sir, and welcome back.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We are going to proceed with your testimony today. I doubt if we will finish today, but we will do our utmost. Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Good morning. Good morning, everyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment, Mr. McCloskey. I only need -- I just wish to remind you -- Witness, I wish to remind you that the solemn declaration that you made when you first started testifying, namely that you will be testifying the truth, still holds good. We don't repeat it each time you walk into the courtroom. It's valid for the entire duration of your testimony. Do you understand me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Witness, I don't have too many more questions for you, but I do want to go back to that day where you said the grave in Glogova was being dug and go over something that you mentioned before. You said that this ULT loader from the brick factory showed up and that you had concerns over it not being able to dig very well. And did you contact anyone regarding that ULT, the problem with the ULT digging?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I told Colonel Beara that this wasn't a place where this machine could be used to dig. I said it wouldn't be able to be done in this way.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Do you remember how you told him? Did you see him in person, did you get him on the phone, did you pass on a message? How did that all happen, if you remember?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I personally told him this in his office when we discussed machinery used for digging.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And what day was that? Was that the day that the digging started or another day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That was when we had this discussion in the office about digging the grave.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. And when you told him about the ULT problems, did he have any solution that he told you about?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. He said that the machine could be used for digging and that I should attempt to do so. We tried to dig, we realised that it wouldn't work, and then I can no longer remember how I informed the Colonel that the machine couldn't be used to dig. He said we should find a -- an excavator from the Zvornik Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. And the day that you began to dig, did an excavator arrive, besides that ULT?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: After I had informed him, after I had briefed the Colonel and told him that this machine couldn't be used, sometime in the evening -- or rather, in the afternoon, from Konjevic Polje -- or rather Kravica, a backhoe excavator arrived in Glogova at the site that was to be dug.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Now, you also mentioned on Friday that bodies were collected by the utility workers up along the road from the Bratunac-Konjevic Polje road. Can you tell us, do you know how many bodies were retrieved from the area of the intersection at Konjevic Polje?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At the crossroads in Konjevic Polje, I think there were between 10 and 15 bodies. I saw this with my very own eyes when I was down there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Can you tell us where it -- at the crossroads, and the Court is, I believe, familiar with that new gas station that's there and the new church that is across the road from the gas station.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At the site in front of the church across the road from the petrol station, that's where it was. I think there were also a few bodies at the location where the petrol station is now situated.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. And along with those 10 to 15 bodies, do you know roughly how many other bodies were collected along the Konjevic Polje-Bratunac road that were brought to Glogova?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know the exact number, but I think --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please repeat the answer?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Witness, you need to repeat your answer because the interpreters couldn't hear you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I said that I don't know the exact number, but I think that a FAB-13 was full -- an FAP-13 was full when it arrived in Glogova. People would load them on manually, those who were responsible for collecting the bodies.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So can you give us a rough figure of how many bodies you think would fit in this FAP-13 truck?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I couldn't say anything off the top of my head. I wasn't paying much attention. I didn't count the bodies, so as these people were dead, I wouldn't like to say anything off the top of my head.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. You had also mentioned on Friday that there were corpses in Bratunac next to the school. Which school are you talking about?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The Vuk Karadzic school, which is across the municipality -- across the road from the municipality building.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. I'm going to show you a diagram that you've seen before. On e-court it's 65 ter 1553. It's an aerial image of Bratunac with some yellow markings that you saw in my office the other day. Did you confirm that those yellow markings indicating various places were the correct locations, they were marked correctly?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. If we can blow this image up to the school complex, which is the series of arrows on the right. Another shot, if you could. Okay. And could I ask you, there is a marker where you can actually mark on this picture. Sorry. She'll take care of you, the usher will take of you on this. And, first of all, can you tell me, did you actually go to the school that day and see bodies?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I didn't go to the school, and I didn't see any bodies in the school.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: How about around the school? Did you actually see some bodies around --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I saw five or six bodies in front of the school. When I say in front of the school, that means by the road in the direction of the municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Can you just put an X where you saw these five or six bodies in front of the school, if you can make it out from this image?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. And could you put your -- your number -- your pseudonym number, which is PW-161, just in the right corner of the image, so that we know that you've done this.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: P?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yeah, PW-161.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And the date, which is 26 March.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And can you tell us what -- what day you saw these five or six bodies by the school? Was it in relation to the day that the -- the grave was begun digging? Was it that day or another day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think it was on that day. But when the digging started on that occasion, these bodies were transported to the grave in Glogova, but Milivoje Cvetinovic, the driver, who had transported the bodies, said there were more bodies than the ones that I had seen, bodies that he had collected.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Did he indicate to you where those additional bodies were located?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. He just said that there were more of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Did he give you any kind of a number or estimate of how many more than the five or six you saw?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: All he said is that there a lot more than the number of bodies I had told him I had seen.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And did you give you any indication where those bodies were collected?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the vicinity of the school.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. I'm through with that image then. We can save that. And how many days, if you know, was the grave at Glogova being dug and having bodies delivered to it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: People from the RAD company and the civilian protection were involved in digging the graves in Glogova. And, as far as I know, they were involved in this for three days.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And how many of those three days were you actually there and present?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was present there on all three days, but I didn't spend the entire day there. I'd go to Bratunac to the company. I was also involved in carrying out other tasks.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Do you know roughly how many pits were dug in this Glogova site?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Four pits were dug. To the left of the road there was one large pit and one small grave and to the right there were two smaller graves.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Can you give us just a rough estimate, if you can, of how many bodies were buried in that grave?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: During the three days while I was down there and while people from the utilities company and the civilian protection were there, I think that between four and 500 bodies were buried, although I believe that other bodies were buried subsequently when I was no longer in the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. And do you have any idea about those -- did you get any reports of how many other bodies were buried at Glogova when you weren't there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. You testified on Friday that you assumed some of those bodies were from Kravica. Can you tell us more definitively what kind of knowledge, if any, you had about bodies from Kravica being buried at Glogova?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, most of the bodies buried in Glogova, I believe, were from Kravica, because vehicles came from the direction of Kravica and I know that people had been killed around the Zadruga Kravica, and those bodies were transported to Glogova. A FAP-13 lorry that was owned by the utilities company was involved in these activities.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: It sounds like you've used a word that I haven't heard before, it may be a translation issue, but you said that the people had been killed around the something in Kravica. Can you tell us what you -- what you said?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I said that I believe that most of the people in -- were -- who were buried in Glogova had been killed in Kravica, because the lorries, one of which was a FAP-13 lorry and was owned by the RAD utilities company in Bratunac, transported these bodies to the site in Glogova.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Does a FAP-13 -- is that a hydraulic dumping ability? Or do you have to unload it by hand?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, the FAP did have this hydraulic mechanism, so it could tip things out.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. And do you recall giving an interview to the OTP in October -- in Banja Luka in October 2000?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And did you -- did you basically provide the same account regarding your contacts with Mr. -- or Colonel Beara as you have today? And yesterday -- and Friday?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: What was different?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, many things.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: But I'm just -- I'm just talking about, did you tell the OTP that you had seen Colonel Beara and that he had sent you to the grave, that basic story, did you tell that to Mr. Ruez in October 2000?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think I did. But the version was a little different. I made quite a few mistakes. Mr. Ruez, in my opinion, didn't interview me in a correct manner. He said when Srebrenica had fallen, he mentioned the excavations, et cetera. I just confirmed the dates, because even now I don't know the dates. I wasn't keeping track of things. If I had known that I'd find myself in such a situation, perhaps I would have kept a diary.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Is it fair to say that in that Banja Luka interview your chronology and your dates were not -- not correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It's not that I became confused, but it has nothing to do with what I told you and what I said on Friday and what I'm saying now. The chronology of events isn't such as it was described, the dates -- well, at the time and when I last testified I also asked everyone not to discuss dates because I really cannot remember any dates.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. And you also testified in April of 2004. Were you able to give the basic -- your basic account of seeing Colonel Beara and going -- going to the Glogova site -- did you testify about that basic information in 2004?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, but again, I made a mistake or I failed to notice something. It appeared that Colonel Beara told me a day before all of that happened that the grave should be dug, but that's not true, that's not how things happened. So that's why I want this to be corrected, what I said to you should be corrected. I don't want to offend anyone. I came here to tell the truth. I don't want any falsehoods to be stated.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So have you had a chance in the last few days to really think about this chronology and get it straight in your mind?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, and what I told you, in fact, represents the actual chronology of events. The events in Glogova -- or rather Kravica.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. And does that include your -- the testimony from Friday and today, does that reflect the proper chronology of events?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. And did you actually help yourself with that chronology by writing out some notes in the last -- well, a few days ago, to help get that chronology straight in your head?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I didn't write out any notes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Well, let me try remind you. Do you remember the -- providing us with some handwritten -- an account, I don't know if notes is the right word, but just a brief chronology to help refresh your recollection about it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. And if you need those -- that outline to help you in any way, just let us know, but did those -- writing it out help you sort out the chronology for your testimony?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. And in the previous trial in 2004 you -- you did testify about seeing the -- the -- I believe the Kravica execution. But you did not tell Mr. Ruez about that in October 2000. Can you tell us, if you know, why you didn't tell Mr. Ruez about the -- about seeing the Kravica execution when you saw him in Banja Luka? I think the same question was asked of you at the last trial.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I didn't tell him about that, because he didn't ask me about it. That's number one. And then secondly, I avoided telling anyone about that because I was quite simply afraid of those stories about killings, about discussing these executions with people who didn't know about them or with people whom I thought did not know about them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you, Witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I have no further questions, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. McCloskey. Who is going first? Mr. Ostojic.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. President. I think I will.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I don't know. I mean usually we let you decide who will go after who.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Then I have decided I will go first.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Mr. Ostojic is lead counsel for Colonel Beara, Witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Witness. Sir, today --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Sir, today we're going to spend a little time discussing these mistakes that you have been kind enough to tell us you've made and why you make these mistakes and I think we all have a theory as to why mistakes are made when recollecting certain facts that may or may not appeared, but before I do that, sir, I would like to ask you a little bit more about your background and I want to talk about 1992. Were you the person who was in charge of the burial operation in 1992 in Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And who put you in charge in 1992 of the burial of -- or the digging of graves and the burial of men in Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The military department of Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Ostojic, I would like you to use your good judgement to identify when we need to go into private session. I, for example, just wish to know whether this question, for example, in itself would identify him to several people.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I'm not sure that it would, but I think we're safe to proceed in open session, but if it's borderline, I will certainly fall back to private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. What do you think, Mr. McCloskey?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: It's -- it's getting close. But, as you know, this is a troublesome area. But I -- I think...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Let's proceed for the time being. Go ahead, Mr. Ostojic. And as I said, please use your good judgement, both of you, and we are at your disposal.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Of course. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Sir, in 1992 when you were in charge of digging of these graves for the burial, can you tell us what ethnic group was buried in those graves in 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And how many people were buried in those graves?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was just one grave, a mass grave. And I believe between a hundred and 150 bodies were buried there all together.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Could you share with us the time of machinery you used in 1992 to bury these Muslim men from Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm afraid I did not understand you. Are you talking about digging the pit itself? When you mention the type of equipment, what did you have in mind? What did you have in mind when you said equipment? Digging the earth or burying the bodies? What did you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Sir, were you in charge of digging the actual graves or the pits, as you call them, in 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Well, what machines or machinery did you use in 1992 to dig these pits?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I believe that it was an ULT machine that we used. It was a loader excavator that was digging that pit in a field on the left-hand side of the Drina.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Was that near or about the area known as Glogova?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, no. It was some 10 or 11 kilometres away from Glogova.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Do you remember, sir, in 2000, after your interview, your first interview with Mr. Ruez, do you remember taking him to a site in Glogova and telling him that this was the same area where Bosnian Muslims were buried in 1992?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: There's no facts in the record regarding that. But I guess the witness can sort it out. I'll withdraw that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think so. Again -- I think so as well. Go ahead, if you can answer that question, Witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You've lost me. Can I hear the question again, please? I'm a bit confused.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I asked you, sir, if you remember, after your interview with Mr. Ruez on October 13th, 2000, did you remember taking him or going with him to a site in Glogova and telling him that this was the same area where Bosnian Muslims were buried in 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: After the interview in Banja Luka, actually a few months later, I went to the Glogova locality with Mr. Ruez, but I never told him that in 1992 Muslim bodies had been buried in Glogova. Because after Glogova I took Mr. Ruez to the locality where the 100 to 150 Muslim bodies had been buried in 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Where were these Bosnian Muslims in 1992, where were they killed? Do you know?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. They were killed in the Vuk Karadzic elementary school.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And that's the same school that the Bosnian Muslims were held or the area where you claim you saw bodies in front of the school in 1995, correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, sir, can you tell me who was in charge of digging the graves in 1995?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: This is getting to the -- a little more close to the problematic area.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: If he thinks so, we can go into private session for this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think so too, actually. I almost -- it's as if he could read my mind. So let's go into private session for a short while.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I will repeat the question, if the Court allows.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Sir, we're back in open session, so we'll be careful, if you don't mind. Can you tell me what your relationship was with Momir Nikolic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, it was a good relationship, a friendly relationship. We were pals, we had grown up in the same town, we had lived close to each other for a number of years. I don't know what else to tell you.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: That's good enough. How about Vidoje Blagojevic, what was your relationship with him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Vidoje Blagojevic is a special story when it comes to our relationship. From the very young age, from the first class of elementary school to the end of the secondary school, we were growing up together, we played together, we went to the military school together. We had an exceptional relationship. We were friends, we were mates, we had an excellent relationship.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Miroslav Deronjic --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Just one moment. Mr. McCloskey, this last statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Again, I think we are all right. There's many people that fit that description, but the answers, of course, are hard to predict.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Go ahead. I apologise to you, Mr. Ostojic.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: That's okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We have an extra job to do. Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Sir, what about Miroslav Deronjic, what was your relationship with him in 1995?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good. Better than the one I had with Momir Nikolic. We were members of the same party, we socialised, we cooperated.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: When you say the same party, would that be the SDS party?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Were you ever a member of the Radical Party?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me what your relationship is with a gentleman by the name of Srbislav Davidovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Extremely good.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. How about Luka Markovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Luka Markovic is nothing but an acquaintance.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. If we can just go into private session to follow up on a couple issues?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Certainly, Mr. Ostojic. Thank you for pointing that out. Let's go into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We are in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Sir, I want to ask you a little follow-up question that was asked today as a result of your testimony on Friday from my learned friend from the Office of the Prosecutor. You said to him that you assumed that the bodies came from Kravica, and then you gave us some explanation today, but my concrete question is this, sir: Were you ever at Kravica and on the premises of the Kravica compound where the massacres occurred?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You mean on the day when the massacre actually took place, whether I was there on the day?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Let's break it down. Any time immediately prior, during or after the massacre at Kravica on the 13th of July, 1995.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Again, I am not discussing any dates, but I was there on that day, actually, I was passing through Kravica on the way to Konjevic Polje, and I did see the killings.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. The incident or killings that you saw, sir, you described that to us. You were in your car, you never left your car, you saw that on the road. My specific question is, were you physically on the Kravica warehouse premises when this incident occurred on that day or any -- or the day after, for example?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: So am I correct, sir, that if people like Momir Nikolic say that they saw you right on the Kravica compound immediately after these incidents at Kravica, they would be mistaken, correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They wouldn't be telling the truth. I don't know whether they would be mistaken. It's up to you to decide.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I will go with not telling the truth, sir. Let me ask you this: What about Ljupko Ilic, what if he said he saw you actually physically on the Kravica compound immediately after the incident that we discussed 13th of July, 1995, would he be, as you said, "wouldn't be telling the truth"? Would he also not be telling the truth if he said that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Ljupko Ilic could have seen me in the compound of the cooperative a few days following the incident when I was in charge of the people who came with the cisterns and they were washing the enclosed area where the people had been interred. He could not have seen me anytime before that and I sincerely doubt that Ljupko was even there around that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Let me ask you about Luka Markovic. What his job, if you remember, in July 1995 at Kravica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Do you know if he was a director or manager of that whole facility or compound?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The director of that cooperative was Jovan Nikolic. It could not have been Luka, what did you say his family name was? He could not have been. Because Jovan Nikolic was the director of that cooperative of that compound.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: The last name just to help you how the out is Markovic. But the question I have to you is this. What if both Jovan Nikolic and Luka Markovic stated that they saw you at the actual compound, Kravica, immediately following the incident that we've described as Kravica, July 13th, 1995. Would they also not be telling the truth, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I've told you once and I'll repeat it. They could have seen me a few days, five or six days after the incident when I was there with some men, with two cisterns, and with the men who were washing the enclosed area. During the actual killings, I told you where I was and I have repeated it again today.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you for that and we'll get to try to put this all in context here for us. Sir, can you --

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: It might be time for the break, but I'm at your disposal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think we can take the break now, yes. Thank you. 25 minutes, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ostojic.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Sir, the last question that we were discussing with you, I believe in open session, was immediately following the incident that we've described as Kravica, July 13th, 1995, if you could just concretely tell us when exactly after you witnessed that incident were you actually on the Kravica compound for the first time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: A minute ago I said, and I'll say it again, as far as the agricultural cooperative is concerned, as far as the Kravica compound is concerned, well I wasn't there, I was at the asphalt road on the way towards Konjevic Polje.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: So -- and I understand that part of your story. But after that day, at any time after that, and I thought you said several days but I wanted to be more precise or as precise as possible. When, if at all, did you actually go on to that Kravica compound where the incident occurred that you witnessed on the 13th of July?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: After that date I didn't go there immediately. But three, four, five days later, that's when I went there. When we were washing the open space where these people had been killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. And I just -- I'm going to direct your attention to your testimony, or your interview that you gave to Mr. Ruez on the 13th of October, 2000. Specifically page 22. You and Mr. Ruez were discussing finding and transporting of the bodies towards Glogova from Kravica. And then he asked you this question on line 5, if I could just read it. It says, "JR --" which I think is Jean-Rene Ruez. "Did you go further than this agricultural complex towards Konjevic Polje or did you stop there and then return to Glogova?" Your answer, sir, on line 7 is, "That day I went only to Kravica." Can you explain to me, sir, why it is, if you were not at Kravica, why did you tell Mr. Ruez that that day the only place you were at was actually Kravica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I haven't understood you very well. If I wasn't in Kravica, why did I say I was only in Kravica? I did tell Mr. Ruez that I had been in Kravica and that I didn't go any further. But I did go to Konjevic Polje on that day when I saw the killings and on the following day, when we did the digging, I also passed through Kravica on that day and continued as far as Konjevic Polje.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Well, just to flush it out, and I'm sorry, but I just have a nagging question about this. Your answer was this: "That day I went only to Kravica." I read that to mean that the only place you were that day, after the incident of the 13th of July, 1995, the only place you were at was at actually the Kravica compound. Am I mistaken in that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You're not mistaken when you say that that's what I told Mr. Ruez. But you showed after the fact that I made a mistake or that I failed to mention something.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. [French on English Channel]?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I told the representative of the Prosecution everything, the whole truth, the entire chronological order of events, so I believe that everything is quite clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: We'll clear it up even further, I hope. Sir, my question to you is did you, -- and we got a note from my learned colleague that you reviewed both your interview with Mr. Ruez got and your proofing note from Mr. Karnavas, as well as your testimony in the Blagojevic case and they were true and accurate. Did you tell that the Prosecutor at any given time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I apologise. Could you repeat that question?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Sure. You had an opportunity to review your statement from Mr. Ruez the 13th of October, 2000, correct? Prior to your testimony here this week?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And you also had an opportunity to review the testimony you gave under oath in the Blagojevic case, (redacted) correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And did you inform the Prosecutor, after reviewing those statements or interviews that you gave, that they were true and accurate?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I told the Prosecution where the mistakes were. I corrected myself and told the entire truth. I told them about what I could remember. I didn't want to speculate about things I could not remember. And I didn't want to make any very rough assessments to say things that weren't true.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Well, share with us, because my learned colleague was kind enough to share one correction that you made, and then changed and then remade again. But sure with us the other mistakes or errors that you found in both your interview as well as your sworn testimony in the Blagojevic case. What did you tell the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Before he answers, Mr. McCloskey and Mr. Ostojic, I am -- don't know if we had agreed on Friday that any reference to the fact that he has testified in Blagojevic was to be in private session. I don't recall really, but perhaps you can think about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We are still in time to redact in any case.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: We should probably just redact the date, but there were many people, obviously, who testified. Just because if we give the day, he did testify on that specific day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's true, Mr. Ostojic, on the other hand, I mean, I don't suppose there are many others who testified on the same substance, same role.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Quite the contrary, Your Honour. But we'll flesh that out in due course. Yes, there were. There were quite a few.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey, you agree with Mr. Ostojic?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: As you can imagine, Bratunac and the goings on was a much bigger issue than it will be at this trial, I hope. So there is -- there is a fair amount of information. But it is -- it's close.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Witness, I was asking you if you could highlight for us some of the discrepancies or mistakes that you found that you shared with the Prosecutor in your interview and your testimony in that other case.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I noticed that there were some erroneous dates. Mr. Ruez conducted the interview. He asked me whether Srebrenica fell on the 11th, I said yes, he said did this happen on the 12th, I said yes, he asked me, did Colonel Beara ask -- phone you at such and such a date, and I said yes. I saw that I had made mistakes as far as those dates are concerned, as far as the chronology of events was concerned or perhaps the chronology of events was not that erroneous, but the dates were completely wrong. And a minute ago I mentioned other things that I had noticed. I noticed that I had stated that Colonel Beara, a day prior to the killings, called me and asked me about the machines and about an order to excavate. But that's not how things happened. Any mistakes I noticed I corrected and we went through the chronology of events with the Prosecution, and we removed the mistakes that had been made.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. And any other mistakes that you can highlight for us that you can recall at this time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can't remember anything else at this point in time. You could put questions to me and then I could answer them.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I appreciate that. I hope to. I found that you had given the Office of the Prosecutor on these issues no less than five or six different versions of your story. Would I be correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Could you tell me which five or six versions you have in mind? I don't know which versions you are referring to, it's not clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Not my versions. They were your versions. For example the first version I that have that you gave to Mr. Ruez on October 13th, 2000, was that you claimed Mr. Beara in your first contact and conversation with him, was before the enclave fell and before the incident at Kravica. The second version that we have is your testimony in that other case in April of 2004, where you changed, ever so slightly, your story and said the conversation happened after the fall of Srebrenica but before the Kravica warehouse incident. Your third version, sir, was just recent when you met with the Prosecutor on March 20th, 2007. At that time you told the Prosecutor, at least from information that they provided to us, that your purported conversation with Mr. Beara was after the enclave fell and after the Kravica incident. That was March 20th, 2007. Then a day later, apparently in another conversation you had with the Prosecutor, the fourth version of your story, you now say that it was before the Kravica killings. That was on March 21st, 2007. And then we have the fifth version of your story, sir, that you testified in part on Friday and here today, Monday, that your meeting and conversation with Mr. Beara was supposedly on -- took place after the incident at Kravica. Can you tell me why, sir, you have so many different versions to this purported meeting that you had with Mr. Beara in July of 1995?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think the third and the fifth version that you have just read out are the same. But why did I make so many things up, well, so many things happened in the war and after the war. And as a result it wasn't possible for me to register many things. If I knew that I'd find myself in this situation, I would have kept records in a different manner. I would have paid more attention to certain facts. But when it comes to Banja Luka and Mr. Ruez, I would be grateful if you didn't put too many questions to me about that. I said that in my opinion, he conducted the interview in a faulty manner, at least in my opinion, he mentioned dates that I would then confirm, so the procedure was chaotic. Later when I read all this through, I realised that there was one mistake after the other.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Well, I can't promise you that I won't go over the Ruez interview, sir. But I can tell you that I find some fault with Mr. Ruez also. However, I can tell you this: That in the interview of October 13th, 2000, Mr. Ruez did not suggest dates to you; it was you, sir, who decided to testify based on events and not dates. It was you who initially, sir, said that the conversation that you had with Mr. Beara was prior to the enclave falling and prior to the incident at Kravica.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When I say that I made a mistake, does that mean anything to you, when I say that that's not correct? It's not correct to say that I provided the dates. Mr. Ruez mentioned the dates and all I did was confirm them.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. Let's for a moment, if you could try to be cooperative with me, forget about the dates. Were you not using certain incidents that occurred in July 1995 as milestones to discuss when something may or may not have happened? For example, for us, it doesn't really matter if the Srebrenica enclave fell on the 5th of July or the 25th of July. The critical point is that the Srebrenica enclave fell, correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's quite natural.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: So when you tell Mr. Ruez that you had the meeting prior to or before the fall of the enclave, it really doesn't matter if Mr. Ruez said it was the 11th, the 12th, or any other date for that matter; isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would now like to ask you, when did Srebrenica fall? Even to this day I don't know whether it was on the 11th or 12th or the 13th.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: We covered that with Mr. Karnavas. The 11th of July, 1995, is the date that we're using as the correct date of the fall of Srebrenica, if I can share that information.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Actually, that's not necessarily correct. The date that Srebrenica fell is -- is debatable.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Fair enough.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: That's part of the problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: We'll move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think let's move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, in your interview with Mr. Ruez, sir, do you remember that you did not tell him that you met Mr. Beara on two occasions but on only one occasion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I remember that we mentioned the fact that I had met him, but as to whether I said it was on one occasion or on two occasions....

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Well, you never mentioned to him that you had this second meeting with him; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Did you tell the Prosecutor how it was that you all of a sudden remembered that there was this supposed second meeting with Mr. Beara at 1.00 or 2.00 in the morning?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, it's not as if I remembered it all of a sudden. It's just that it's not something I mentioned to Mr. Ruez.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Because he failed --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This isn't the first time I told the Prosecution about that. I also mentioned the fact that at the Blagojevic hearing when I testified.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Is it your testimony that Mr. Ruez didn't ask you if you had more than one contact with Mr. Beara on or about July 1995?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, he didn't ask me about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I suggest to you, sir, that you told Mr. Ruez, that after the first contact you had with Mr. Beara that you saw him in the following days only once, and it was maybe two or three days after your first meeting. Do you remember discussing that at all with Mr. Ruez?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: In fact, sir, you told Mr. Ruez that very thing, did you not? That you only had one contact with Mr. Beara and the next time that you saw him and did not have contact with him was two or three days later at the Hotel Fontana, correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm not denying having said that to Mr. Ruez. But I'm saying that I made some mistakes as far as the order of events was concerned, as far as whom I saw when and where. I didn't mention the certain meeting and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Well, sir, it's more than just that you didn't mention it, you told Mr. Ruez specifically the next time you had contact with Mr. Beara, after the first contact, was two or three days later when you just happened to see him at the Hotel Fontana, correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I didn't say that we had contact. I had just seen the Colonel in the Fontana Hotel. We didn't have any contact, though.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: According to my review and study of your versions of this story, the first time you mentioned this second purported meeting with Mr. Beara was to the Blagojevic Defence team, correct? Four years after Mr. Ruez's interview with you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Let's focus a little bit our attention on the meeting or meetings you had with the Defence team of Mr. Vidoje Blagojevic. How many times did you meet with them or any member of their team prior to your testimony?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Do you know if it was more than five times?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know. I didn't keep any records.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Was Mr. Celanovic ever present during any of your meetings with the Blagojevic Defence team?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: How about Mr. Davidovic, was he present, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is all new, what you're asking me about, whether someone was with me or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I know. I think of myself as being somewhat unique and original from time to time. But let me ask you an open-ended question: Who, if anyone else from Bratunac, was present at the meetings that you were at with the Defence team of Mr. Blagojevic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You mean here in The Hague or when they went to Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. Let's start with here in The Hague in 2004.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I was on my own. No one was ever with me when I had meetings with the Blagojevic Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: How about back in Bratunac, who was with you when you met with the Defence team --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't think anyone was present with me in Bratunac, either. That's why you confused me when you asked me about who was present at those meetings. Only I was present in The Hague and I think that was also in -- the case in Bratunac. One or two occasions -- well, on one occasion I think Mr. Karnavas was present and I was alone with Ms. Suzana.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Prior to interviewing or giving an interview with Mr. Ruez in October of 2000, did you discuss the prospects of your interview with anyone?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. Prior to you being called as a Defence witness in the Blagojevic case, did you discuss your testimony with anyone other than the Defence team of Mr. Blagojevic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, there were discussions with Mr. Deronjic, with Mr. Momir Nikolic, because they had been in Banja Luka before me. I asked them whether I was mentioned in any sort of context, they said no, no one has mentioned you. So I was a little angry with them, because they didn't say that I had been mentioned, that my name had been mentioned down there.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And just so I have it right, was this meeting or these discussions that you had with Mr. Deronjic and Mr. Nikolic, did that occur also prior to your giving an interview to Mr. Ruez in October of 2000?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, because they had seen Mr. Ruez before me.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And that's what I thought, but I want to make sure it's clear. Because in -- on page 48, lines 8 through 10, when I asked you what I thought was that question, you answered a certain way, but we can move on. Sir, isn't it true that prior to your interview on the 13th of October --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can't hear.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I'll try to speak louder. Prior to your interview with Mr. Ruez on the 13th of October, 2000, you met with Mr. Nikolic to discuss what it was that you were going to testify about, correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. I met with Mr. Nikolic, and I asked him about what we were discussing a minute ago. I asked him whether anyone had mentioned my name, and if so, in what context my name had been mentioned. He said no one had mentioned it. I didn't -- I hadn't received a summons to testify, I didn't even know I would be coming here at the time. Rather, when I spoke to Mr. Nikolic on that occasion, I didn't know that I would be going to Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And how many days prior to the interview with Mr. Ruez did you speak with Mr. Nikolic? Momir Nikolic, just so the record is very clear.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can't remember. All I know is that when I came from Banja Luka, I phoned Mr. Nikolic and asked him to come and see me in my office. I told him that Mr. Ruez sent his greetings and I asked him why he hadn't responded to the second summons. He said he hadn't received it. And that's what happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Just -- let me read this out to you from your interview with Mr. Ruez. On page 33, for my learned friend. On line 19 -- I'll strike that. On line 22 again Mr. Ruez asked you, "Did you meet him," meaning Mr. Momir Nikolic, "at any moment during the days we discussed here? Momir Nikolic," is exactly what's written. Your answer on line 24 and 25, sir, said, "I didn't see him but the answer was I saw him three days ago. We were having coffee." This is from your interview of the 13th of October, 2000. Is it true, is all I'm asking you, sir, that you actually saw and met with Mr. Momir Nikolic three days prior to your interview on the 13th of October, 2000?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, okay. Let's say three days, four days. If I said I had coffee, that's probably true.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, tell me how many days prior to your interview with Mr. Ruez in October 2000 did you meet with Mr. Deronjic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Was anyone else present with you and Mr. Nikolic three days prior to your interview with Mr. Ruez?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm not sure, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Sir, in your interview on the 13th of October, am I correct that you denied that you were given a request to collect bodies of prisoners who had been killed in and around the detention facilities in the Bratunac town, did you not? You denied that, correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Please repeat.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Sure. In your interview of the 13th of October, 2000, you at that time, sir, denied that you were given a request to collect bodies of prisoners who had been killed in and around the detention facilities in Bratunac town, correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Request if that is -- it's got a line and page for that, I would appreciate it being used because it does not -- it's not a reflection of my recollection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's fair enough. I'm sure Mr. Ostojic can do that. Yes, Mr. Ostojic.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I could, but I would first like to hear the answer from the witness. But if the Court wants me to do it the reverse order, I'll do it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The question is that the opposite party, Mr. McCloskey, ought to be in the position to follow the witness's answer. After that, he has been directed to the -- to the reference. I mean --

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Fair enough.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: -- of course you will repeat your question and without any discussions taking place, he can refer to the excerpt.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Page 11, lines 20 through 23.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Can you answer my question, sir? I've asked it twice. Do you want me to ask it again?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: He is waiting for the interpretation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Who is waiting for the interpretation? I see. I think you need to repeat your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I will.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, I think for everybody's benefit.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: For the third time, Mr. Witness, in your interview on the 13th of October, 2000, did you at that time deny that you were given a request to collect bodies of prisoners who had been killed in and around the detention facilities in Bratunac town?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Why don't you read out the question and the answer that he gave.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I'll explain it quite candidly, Your Honour, because I think it's important that these issues we specifically hear from the witness first in order to be able to weigh and evaluate his credibility, quite candidly, but I'll read it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: He's answered you in the sense he you doesn't recall, so --

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. Fair enough.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, to refresh your recollection, sir, if we could have 1D167 on the ELMO, page 11. While that's coming up, maybe I can ask another question, because it comes right after that, if you don't mind.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: If you have the text in front of you, I don't think we need to see it. If you read it slowly, then it can be interpreted and we don't need to waste time to have it uploaded.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Sir, here is the question Mr. Ruez asked you in October 2000, "In Bratunac town, did you have any request also to, had the RAD, R-a-d, company also requested to collect the bodies of prisoners who had been killed in and around the detention facilities in Bratunac town?" End quote for Mr. Ruez. Your answer on line 23, "No." Do you remember telling him that, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is possible, if this has been recorded in this particular way, I must have, if this is what it says.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: It is what -- it is what it says, but, sir, can you tell us why you were mistaken or why you didn't tell Mr. Ruez the truth about the bodies of prisoners that had been killed in and around the detention facilities in Bratunac town?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Objection. That statement is actually -- does not fit the evidence, if we go farther into the interview.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. I don't think any of us is in a position to control that. What do you wish to state on that, Mr. Ostojic? And if necessary, we can ask the witness to remove his headphones while we discuss this.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I totally disagree with my learned friend. If he wants and has an opportunity on redirect, he can flesh all these issues out, which he may have -- and should have done possibly when he met with the witness and before in doing his direct testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The objection actually goes to the correctness of your question in the first place. In other words, it's being submitted to you that what -- the way you have framed your question does not fit the evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. I'll restate it if the Court feels that way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's have it rephrased and we see whether Mr. McCloskey still objects to it. Otherwise, if we need to discuss it, we will need to discuss it without the presence of the Witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: In fact, sir, I suggest to you that you told Mr. Ruez on the 13th of October, 2000, that as far as you knew, there were no bodies there in Bratunac, did you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Well, let's look at 1D167 again. Same page, very next question from Mr. Ruez after you denied that you were given a request to collect bodies of prisoners who had been killed in or around the detention facilities in the Bratunac town. Mr. Ruez asked you this: "There was no request to collect anybody from the Bratunac town?" Your answer, starting on line 25, "In Bratunac, no. As far as I know, there were no bodies there." You go on to give other testimony, but I wanted to focus on that. Do you remember telling Mr. Ruez that, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is possible that I did, if this is what it says in here.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Sir, can you reconcile that for us? How it is that in October 2000 you tell Mr. Ruez as far as you knew, there were no bodies in Bratunac, and then in your testimony here last week that you were actually collecting bodies from the Bratunac town?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Objection. The implication in that question does not reflect the reality of the interview.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And, Madam Usher -- I think we need to hear more on this, unless you wish to rephrase your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I refuse to rephrase my question, unless the Court directs me to do so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I'm just asking you for the time being, but we need to hear more on this because this is a viva voce witness, so we don't come here having read or previous testimonies or statements, we prefer not to. So I think, Madam Usher, you need to ask the witness to remove his headphones, please. And, yes, Mr. McCloskey, could you be more specific, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. I would direct everyone to page 35, where near the end of this interview where there is a discussion of bodies in Bratunac and that he did say that he got a call to collect bodies from Bratunac. So I have no problem with specific questions regarding the first part that he is talking about, but to imply that he never said anything about bodies from Bratunac until he came to testify would be incorrect. In my view of -- based on what you can see from page -- page -- the end of the interview, page 35. I have no problems with questions on either of those points, but what I think -- I'm -- try to make myself clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ostojic.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: If I could have a line reference, that might help.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, I'm sure he will give you that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Page 35, line 25, and after talking about Bratunac and bodies, he specifically says, "I was told on the phone to collect bodies from the hangar. Whether they were killed there or not, I didn't know."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ostojic.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I think, if we flesh it out with the witness, you'll find, and I think my learned friend will agree with me, that in 1992 the bodies of Bosnian Muslims were taken from the hangar and that's the reference made to that. They were taken from the Vuk Karadzic hangar, and I will put the question to the witness specifically.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, then -- yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Just read -- read the page, and -- because they're talking, as far as I can see, about the Kravica agricultural complex and Colonel Beara, and I don't think -- hope that agricultural complex was not involved in 1992. .

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PROST
utterances.text: Could we have the page up, please, on the screen?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Do you still maintain that there is doubt, reading through this page, that the witness could have been talking about 1992 events and not 1995 events, the July 1995 events?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I think that I can put the question with your permission to the witness, so we can clarify, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But you put that question first and not the one --

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: -- you put before, in which case if he answers affirmatively, then the previous question will not stand. We need to give the witness his statement in B/C/S. Do we have it? Can it be -- come up on the screen or not? Okay. So -- same page, 35. Yeah, okay. So, Witness, look at me. I would like you to concentrate on the monitor in front of you where a particular page from your interview with Mr. Ruez should show up. We'll give you time to read that page entirely, please. And then Mr. --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is not in Serbian.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I know. It should -- what I -- what I -- yeah. You have to wait a little bit.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: My microphone is not working but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Try it again.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I'm afraid it won't be the same page, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: It's page 39.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Page 39. It's page 39. I thank you, Madam Fauveau.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Did you have an opportunity, sir, to review that page?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I want to know -- if I could proceed, Mr. President. I want to know concretely from you, sir, were you told to collect the bodies from the hangar at the Vuk Karadzic School, or only those that you said earlier were laying around the school or lying around the school?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your previous question was whether somebody ordered me to collect the bodies in Bratunac. I said no. And the fact is that they didn't, because when you say Bratunac, it's a very general term. As for the courtyard of the Vuk Karadzic School where I saw five or six bodies, the driver who collected the bodies, together with some men from RAD Bratunac company, he told me that there had been a lot more bodies than that. I said this to the Prosecutor, I adhered by that. Your previous question was whether somebody had instructed me to collect bodies around Bratunac, and I know nobody did. Nobody ever said anything about any bodies in the -- in the Bratunac area, because there were none. The only bodies were in the courtyard of the school; that's where the bodies were.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Just so that we're clear, we're talking about the school in Bratunac called the Vuk Karadzic School, correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now -- and we're also talking specifically about a hangar that I think we saw in that picture that you were shown during your direct exam today. There is a hangar right behind the Vuk Karadzic School, correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Well, let me ask you this: Were you told to collect the bodies from the hangar of the Vuk Karadzic School in Bratunac in July of 1995?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know. I'm not sure whether the hangar of the school came up. The only thing that was ever said was to collect the bodies around the school.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. Let me ask you this: Do you remember telling Mr. Ruez, and this is page 9, for my learned friend, lines 21 through 23, and it's also in the April 21st, 2004 proofing notes offered by the Defence of Mr. Blagojevic. Do you remember telling Mr. Ruez and Mr. Karnavas that Mr. Beara instructed you to collect both Serb and Muslim dead bodies?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, I said that Colonel Beara had told me that there would be dead. I can't quote my words exactly. He said that there would be dead. When he was asked -- when I was asked either by the Prosecutor or by the Defence whether he had ever said who the dead people would be, in other words, whether it would be Serbs or Muslims, I replied that this was never specified. Nobody ever said who the dead people would be, whether they would be Serbs or Muslims or whoever.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. Let's look at 1D168, which is the proofing note from the 21st of April, 2004.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And it should not be published, Your Honour, because it does contain the names.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you, Mr. Ostojic.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. If we can have the English version as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: It's a one-page document, sir. Do you see where you mention that to Mr. Karnavas at all on that April 21st, 2004 proofing note? It's at the bottom of the page in B/C/S, as well as in English. You see where it starts there with -- right under -- in the last paragraph it says, "Colonel Beara told him that he had to prepare graves in Milici at the Boskit mine that is located there, that Serbian and Muslim casualties were expected." Do you see that? Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Is that incorrect or correct, sir, that you told the Defence lawyers for Mr. Blagojevic that very fact?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm not sure. This must be a mistake. I believe it's a mistake.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. Another mistake. Let's go to the actual meeting or prior to the meeting you claim that occurred with Mr. Beara. I'd like to know, sir, given your five or so different versions of when that happened, not the date of the meeting but if you could be as precise as possible with us, if it happened after the incident at Kravica or before.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It happened on the day. When the incident in Kravica happened, on that same evening, the meeting took place as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, can you tell us specifically, or let me ask it this way: Isn't it true, at least according to a version of your story, that you received a call at your office sometime after 9.00 or 10.00 and you were informed that, "Some representatives of the army of Republika Srpska," wanted you to come to the SDS offices of Miroslav Deronjic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, this is not what I stated. This was Miroslav Deronjic's office, but Miroslav Deronjic was not up there when I entered.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. I was going to ask you that as well. Who else was at this meeting other than yourself and purportedly Mr. Beara, two army officers who you did not get introduced to and did not know their name, and the two purported military policemen who were standing at the front of the SDS offices? Who else was there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Nobody.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Do you know where Mr. Deronjic was that night? Did you see him around at all?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I didn't see him, and I didn't know where he was. I saw him before that but not after.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Before in what, a day or two, or before when?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Before the meeting. I saw him before the meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. And how about Mr. Momir Nikolic, did you see him during some of those what I call critical days, the 11th, 12th, 13th, 14th of July? Did you see him anywhere?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Three or four days or maybe a couple of days. I'm not sure. But as for Momir Nikolic, I did not see him at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. What about Mr. Simic, did you see him on the 13th, the day that you had this purported meeting with Mr. Beara? Did you see him that day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Are you referring to Ljubisa Simic, maybe?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I am.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I did not see him.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Tell me, with the best of your recollection, sir, when you received the call to go to the SDS offices, who called you and what was said?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was called from the building of the municipality. And I was told that I should report to the SDS offices, as Colonel Beara was expecting me there. Because he needed to talk to me, supposedly.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Who called you, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, sir, do you remember that you told Mr. Ruez on October of 2000, on page 10, lines 19 through 22, that you were, in fact, not specifically told that you were going to go see Mr. Beara but -- and I'll read it to you. You state -- I have the wrong document.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Pardon me, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
