utterances.text: You state at line 19, after he asks you a question, you state, "Actually" -- you state on so it's clear again, page 10, on line 19, "Actually whether I was personally informed or someone phoned me, I cannot recall. But I know that someone told me that I should go to the office of the SDS and that I should meet some representatives of the army of the Republika Srpska." Your recollection, I suggest, sir, in 2000, was that you were simply called and you were asked to come to the SDS offices. Now you're telling us that you were told specifically that you should go see Mr. Beara in the SDS offices. Can you reconcile the two for me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know how to explain. Let me ask you this: Would you really believe that I went up there just like that, without any prior invitation, without anybody asking me to go there?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I suggest to you, sir, that the meeting that you claim happened with Mr. Beara never happened, and that the reason that you have so many versions of not just one aspect of your story, but multiple aspects, is that that meeting never occurred. You did not meet with and did not talk to Mr. Beara on or about July 13th, 1995, after the Kravica incident. That's what I'm suggesting to you, sir.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Do you think that I'm lying here before this Court? I came here to testify honourably, to tell the truth. Since you have mentioned this, tell me, why, in your opinion, did I invent this order of events and this meeting with Colonel Beara?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, I'd be delighted to tell you what I think, but I think the Court probably would -- or would rather have me reserve that until the closing argument or after you have concluded testifying. I'm, sir, telling you this: You didn't see Nikolic at all during that time. Are you familiar that Momir Nikolic claims that he talked to you and he was with you both at Glogova and at the Kravica compound? Do you remember being asked those questions in the Blagojevic trial?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as Momir Nikolic is concerned, well, that's completely false. As far as the school goes, I said there were 80 or 100 people buried in Halolovici, et cetera. Perhaps Momir acted in this way, but it is the first time I have aheard about this from his statements.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. Let 's talk about this Luka Markovic again, and I'm going to ask the Court if I can place it on the ELMO, that specific statement, which is not on e-court, but we do have an ERN number, which starts on 0615-9261 through 0615-9267 and we'll be focusing on just quickly two specific pages, if the Court doesn't mind?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Go ahead, Mr. Ostojic.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And we should not publish this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I quite agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Sir, I know that you said that Mr. Nikolic's recollection was -- I think you said was an untruth or a lie, but we have it on the record. I want to ask you about Mr. Luka Markovic. Do you see his statement in front of you on the ELMO, sir?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Maybe a little lower so we can see his name.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Do you see his name there, Luka Markovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And if we go to the next page, or the second to the last page of that document -- I'm sorry?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We are seeing the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I know. If I can have the document and then I can perhaps -- it's my fault, Your Honour, because I failed to put that document in e-court because I wasn't sure what the witness would say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Is there a B/C/S translation of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Not in my possession, Your Honour, but I'm sure it exists. But we'll direct -- we can read it, it's very quick.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I still say let's put it on the ELMO again.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Once more and you direct us to the relevant part.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I will.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And you read it out in a -- slowly so that it can be follow by the interpreters and then you put your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: If we can scroll to the bottom so that we could have a frame of reference.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: "On the 14th of July, in the morning at about 400 hours a column of vehicles went by on the asphalt road from the direction of Kravica towards Konjevic Polje." Just putting in that context, sir, if we can continue on and to the very next page at the top, we're still talking about the 14th of July, 1995, and at 6.00 in the morning, while at this cooperative, if we could move it over to the left a little. Mr. Markovic states the following:" That same morning, at around --"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Just make sure that you don't mention the witness's name.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Of course not, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: That same morning at around 6.00 a.m., 600 hours, the director, another individual, and you, sir, apparently were at the cooperative with 17 other workers. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. Can you tell us, sir, truthfully now, whether or not you were at the Kravica cooperative or compound at 6.00 a.m. On the 14th of July, 1995?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was never with these two individuals at 6.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: That's all we'll need with that document, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, is it your belief -- well, that's true. We always -- when -- were you there by yourself, if not with these individuals at 6.00, sir, on the 14th of July, 1995?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Well, why do you think Mr. Luka Markovic would say something like that unless it were true?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know. I can't understand that.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Sir, is it true that the phone call that you got, it was never mentioned to you when you were going to go purportedly meet Mr. Beara, that you were supposed to go meet Mr. Beara, they only told you that were you going to meet some representatives of the army of Republika Srpska, correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I haven't understood you very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... The first phone call that you got, which informed you to go to the SDS offices, am I correct, sir --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: -- That during that phone call no one ever mentioned the name of Mr. Beara, and that you were asked simply to go to the SDS offices to meet with some representatives of the army of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think Colonel Beara's name was mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. Let's look at the second version of your story, or that you recall, which was given four years after your interview with Mr. Ruez, and your meeting with Mr. Nikolic and Deronjic. This is April 21st, 2004. Now, at that time, sir, you claimed that your first contact and conversation with Mr. Beara was after the fall of the enclave, but before the killings at Kravica warehouse. So I suppose that that would be, given those time-lines, somewhere between July 11th, and 13th, 1995?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Could we have a line and -- page and line where that is stated?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I'm sure he has.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I do, but I quite frankly, Your Honour, think objection is inappropriate. It is throughout the testimony in Blagojevic where this witness repeatedly confirms and reiterates that the sequence, or version of events under oath at that time was that he saw purportedly Mr. Beara before Kravica. So I take some offence that my learned friend is putting us to the task when he very well knows that when their team was in fact cross-examining this very witness on those points. (redacted)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We will redact line 17 on page 66, and the last three words on line 16, of line 16.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We can leave it actually because it's a proofing note.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So we'll make the necessary redaction. Let's make this clear, and I think it applies across the board to everyone. Irrespective of whether the -- your counterpart stands up and says, counsel, I would like to have the exact reference, sometimes you have that, sometimes you don't. But the thing is this, that we also need to be in a position to follow. So -- and it would help us immensely even if you are not asked from the other -- other party, to give the correct reference, that you still give it. And this will apply to everyone and not just to you in the purpose of this case. I mean, as you go along, we are trying to follow, not only the content of the witness's answers, but also other considerations that, as judges, we are bound to make as we go along. So -- and I'm sure that you understand what I'm saying and you will all comply. Thank you, Mr. Ostojic.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Sir, Mr. Witness, do you remember testifying in Blagojevic or Blagojevic that you first went from Glogova, then to Konjevic Polje, and then you saw the killings at Kravica? (redacted)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, please redact, Madam Registrar. All right. Because we are in open session. And if you give the reference to the page number, et cetera, you have practically identified the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Right. Well, okay. Fair enough.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: If you want, we can go into private session. I mean, it's no problem with us. If it makes your life easier. We hate interrupting. It's not in our style, you know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I understand that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: If you think we can safely go into private session and go through this, we will do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: No, I only just gave the reference as a result of the Court's -- Court thing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: In this case it would identify the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So we can redact that and proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Sir, do you remember giving that testimony?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do remember. A minute ago I apologised for this mistake. And I mentioned the fact that I had corrected the mistake. When I gave a statement to the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: So although we're only on the second version of your story, sir, the first version to Mr. Ruez, was a mistake, you were wrong, even though, as the Court will see, on seven different occasions you are the one who put these time-lines to Mr. Ruez specifically, that it was before the fall of the enclave, and before the Kravica incident, and you were also mistaken and wrong, sir, in the testimony that you gave in the Blagojevic case? Am I correct to understand that?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Objection. This is getting argumentative because it's so broad and vague about where he's wrong, and listing it like this it's not really leading us anywhere.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I have a feeling the witness can answer that question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's see if he can answer the question. If then he considers the -- your question vague in any part, we'll deal with that. But he said -- he can certainly address the Blagojevic testimony without any difficulty, I suppose.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] A minute ago I said that I had apologised because of that mistake. I explained to the Prosecution what the situation was, and I told the Prosecutor the truth.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Were you also wrong in that testimony, sir, when you said that you were at -- again on the same page we referenced earlier, "I went from Glogova to Konjevic Polje because a unit from the utilities company was out there on the field. There were a couple of people there who were collecting bodies with several people from the utilities company and the company's truck. They were collecting bodies of the people who had been killed. So I went to Konjevic Polje too, to see what was going on, more out of curiosity. I saw in Kravica a site that I will never forget. I saw the killing." Do you remember giving that testimony in Blagojevic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, what were you doing in Glogova prior to the Kravica incident of July 13th, 1995?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's when I went and there was a team in the field gathering, or rather collecting the bodies. That was the day on which we were digging in the area. That's not when I passed by and saw that sight.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Just so I'm clear, was that a day or two before the Kravica incident?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That was the day after the events in Kravica when the team was in Konjevic Polje and was collecting the dead.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Did you, sir, at any time go to Glogova prior to the Kravica incident of the 13th of July, 1995?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, further on in your testimony in Blagojevic you state, do you not -- and we can maybe go into private so I can give my learned friends the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's go into private east.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: You further on in that testimony, state that the event in Kravica that you described and saw, occurred the day after the machine started operating in Glogova. Do you remember that at all, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Could you please repeat the question?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Sure. In your testimony in Blagojevic you state, sir, that the event in Kravica you saw and described, occurred the day after this machine started operating in Glogova, correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In Kravica there was this event that I witnessed, the day before the machine started operating in Glogova.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I understand that's what your version is now, but in the Blagojevic case did you not, sir, testify under oath that there were machines already that were operating at Glogova prior to the Kravica incident?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can't remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Well, I just read it to you. And that will be fair enough, we can move on to -- and again, just for the Court's reference, it was the most recent one in private session that we talked about. Can you tell me, sir, why there would have been machines operating in Glogova prior to the Kravica incident?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Ostojic --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Foundation. It reverses what he said happened.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I will consult with my colleagues.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We think that Mr. McCloskey is right. You can rephrase your question, if you wish. But It doesn't tally with what he testified a few moments ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, in your testimony, which was the second version of how this contact purportedly with Mr. Beara occurred, you had said there, and I apologise for summarising it, but to put it in proper context for you, sir, you testified that the meeting took place after the fall of the enclave, but before the incident at Kravica. Do you remember that at all?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'll repeat this.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I'm not asking you --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Please. I was then in Kravica and I saw that sight, and on that day, or rather that evening, there was this meeting with Colonel Beara.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. How about on March 21st, 2007, when you met with my learned friend, didn't you tell him at that time also that you saw the executions at Kravica the day after you met with Mr. Beara for the first time? Do you remember telling him that at as well? Sir? Do you remember telling him that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Do you mean now? I didn't understand your reference to this learned friend.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: It's just a words of endearment that we have for each other here in the courtroom. Sir, I'm asking you this: On the 21st of March, 2007, less than five days ago, isn't it correct that you told the Prosecutor that you saw the executions at Kravica the day after you met Mr. Beara for the first time? Did you tell the Prosecutor that or not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I met Mr. Beara on the very same day, or rather in the evening, when this murder in Kravica occurred, or rather what I saw.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, with all due respect, I would like an answer to my specific question. And if -- perhaps if the Court puts it to him the witness would be more willing to answer the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You put it to him again and tell him where he hasn't answered your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Sir, I know what your story or version of your story is now, but I'm asking you, five days ago, sir, did you tell the Office of the Prosecutor that you saw the executions at Kravica the day after you had met with Mr. Beara for the first time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. And afterwards, immediately afterwards, I amended my statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Immediately afterwards meaning the next day, correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: That doesn't reflect the proper sequence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. If it's necessary, I think the -- the -- well, I mean the question is whether it was the next day or not. And he can answer whether it was indeed the next day or not and I think it will clear up the -- your objection. Yes, Witness, can you answer Mr. Ostojic's question, please? And then we will have a break. You said --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think it was in the afternoon on the very same day, but we did meet again on the following day. I think the Prosecutor has the relevant material.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. We can stop there, have a break. So we will have a 25-minute break. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. We'll need 10 minutes at the end for something that we'd like to deal with. Yes, Mr. Ostojic.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Sir, I've asked that the notes of your meeting with the Office of the Prosecutor on the 21st of March of this year be placed on e-court, so if we can please have 2D86, just so we can clarify a couple of points with you. And just at the -- and I think if we can be kind enough just so we could keep it in proper context, just quickly flip to the second page so that we can see from whom this letter is written by. Okay. And it's dated the 21st of March, 2007, thank you. If we could go back to the first paragraph of that exhibit 2D86. Now, here, sir, during your meeting with Mr. McCloskey and the Prosecution staff, you again said that you saw the executions the day after you met Colonel Beara for the first time. My question to you, sir, is the following in connection with that: And that is, what occurred on the days prior that made you rethink and then state to the Prosecutor that you saw the executions the day after you met with Mr. Beara for the first time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I believe that I have already answered that once.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I don't believe, with all due respect, that you have, but if you have, maybe you can just be kind enough to repeat then what had happened that caused you to change the chronology, if you will, or the sequence of events on the 21st of March, 2007 in connection with your purported meeting with Mr. Beara.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The reason was that I realised that I had made a mistake in my first statement, and that the meeting took place on the same evening when the incident i.e., the killings in Kravica had happened, the ones that I had seen.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I know that's what you're saying now, sir, but try to focus, if you will, with me. I know we've had a long day. But on the 21st of March, my learned friend advises us that you told him that the executions at Kravica occurred the day after you met with Mr. Beara for the first time. And recently you testified again under oath that the purported meeting with Mr. Beara for the first time occurred after the Kravica incident and not before. Without giving me the date, sir, can you reconcile for me why, as recently as five or six days ago you, in fact, told the Prosecutor that the executions at Kravica occurred the day after you met with Mr. Beara for the first time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mistake. It was a mistake in my statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Which statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the statement that I -- that the meeting with Colonel Beara took place one day prior to the events in Kravica. This was the mistake, because the meeting took place on the same evening, on the evening of the incident in Kravica.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: We'll move on from that, I think. Can you tell me, sir, being under oath here, on the 21st of March, 2007, five days ago, did you ever tell the Prosecutor that, in fact, in the mid-afternoon on the 14th of July, you went to the Kravica warehouse?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You mean a day after the executions in Kravica. I did. I went through Kravica and through Konjevic Polje on the following day.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And I heard that testimony. I'm asking you, did you tell the Prosecutor that you were actually at the Kravica warehouse, not through Konjevic Polje and through the Kravica, but were you specifically at the Kravica warehouse that next day? Isn't that what you told him?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: He keeps going over this, that's what he just said was a mistake. That 21st statement about Kravica. And it's just -- we're just churning it into more and more confusion. But he's clearly answered that question already.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I respectfully don't agree at all. This is the first time we're using the 21st March 2007 proofing note that we received and the only aspect that we touched on it was the first paragraph and logically we're going to go through to the fifth paragraph where that's said. He has given testimony specifically as to whether or not he claims he was at Kravica and I just want it know how -- I'm going to follow up with questions in that regard.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I think it's very fair.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: He's explained that the 21st statement was a mistake.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I would--

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: He's got that--

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now I'm going through --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I don't want him to go --

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I'm going through --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: -- through something that he says is a mistake --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Stop, stop, stop --

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: If I can --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: -- stop, stop, stop, stop, stop. One moment. I don't -- I can address the -- myself to the witness straight away. Witness, could you kindly remove your ear-phones for a short while, please, while we discuss this. Your headphones. Sorry. Now, let's go through this and please try not to overlap. You are both talking at the same time. Yes, Mr. Ostojic.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, the only reason I tried to interrupt my learned friend is to ask that very thing, that the earphones of the witness be removed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Because I think in the objection there was this -- I would also ask that my learned friend share with us the specific page number and line number where he says that it was clearly answered that question already. He says that on page 76, lines 17 and 18. I don't believe it's correct. I don't believe we've ever touched on this document here today at all. I think that I should be given an opportunity to flesh this out and also ask follow-up questions, specifically why it was that he said that. If he claims that it's a mistake, I want to know how he made that mistake five days ago and changed from what his prior statements, testimony, interviews, conferences with multiple people were.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: He must have asked that same question many times already. We're going just around and around and around, and I just don't see it's getting us anywhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: If we could just have the page cite, Your Honour, we'll look at it as quickly at possible and the line, we would appreciate it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's page 76 and -- yes. That's where Mr. McCloskey stated he is clearly -- that the witness has clearly answered the question already and -- immediately after you disagreed. Let me confer with my colleagues, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So, we intend to try and bring this to an end, because in a way we have been going through this for too much of a long time and there has been repetitive questions and repetitive answers. So let's do it this way: You -- you will refer the witness to the 21st March statement, or proofing note.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Proofing notes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Proofing notes, okay. And specifically put to the witness whether it's correct that on that particular day he stated the following, and you need to tell him what, according to the document, the proofing notes, he is supposed to have stated to the OTP. Then your next question ought to be whether that is a correct information that he gave to the OTP or whether it's not correct. And depending on what the answer is, if he answers you that it was not a correct information that he gave to the OTP on that occasion, you have every right to ask him why. But that's about it. Otherwise, he has already testified on what happened and when he passed -- when he went to Kravica, when he -- so stick to the 21st March proofing notes, and follow the following -- the trail that I indicated to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you for your assistance, Your Honour. May I, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, by all means.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, directing your attention specifically to the 21st of March, 2007, five days ago, is it correct, sir, that you told the Prosecutor, on the 21st of March, 2007, the following, and I'll quote, although this is a summary by the Prosecutor, but following the Court's instructions. "In the mid-afternoon that same day the witness," that would be you, sir, "went to the Kravica warehouse and witnessed the execution he described in his earlier testimony." It appears, I think if we scroll down just a little further, the Court can see it. Right there is fine. It's in that paragraph in the middle of the paragraph where it starts with, "In the mid-afternoon."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I've just told you. I went from Glogovic [as interpreted] via Kravica to Konjevic Polje, and in Kravica I saw the killings within the compound of the agricultural facility, in front of the building.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Sir, all I'm asking you is five days ago did you tell the Prosecutor that, in fact, you were -- went to the Kravica warehouse?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't remember having said that I entered the warehouse. I said that I passed by the warehouse, that I saw the killings on the day when they took place in Kravica.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Well, where do you think the Prosecutor would have come up with this fact that you told him you went to the Kravica warehouse? Would you know?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Objection. That's assuming facts that are not in the -- not in the proofing note, and not in the answer to his question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think the objection has to be sustained. Next question, Mr. Ostojic.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Sir, last Friday when you were about to finish testifying you said that there were, on page 20, lines 1 through 5, that there were a group of workers from the utility company collecting corpses next to the road. Do you remember testifying about that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When -- when was that? And what are you saying? When did I testify about that? On Friday or the prior evidence that I provided?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Friday, March 23rd, 2007.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Last Friday.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I think my question before that specifically said "last Friday," Your Honour, so that's why I thought he might need the date. Fair enough.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The workers from the utility company were collected, corpses by the road from Kravica to Konjevic Polje. On the day when we were digging graves or a grave in Glogova.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Was that the utility company that is called R-a-d, RAD, correct? That's where these group of workers are from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: These workers were not the employees of RAD. Some of them were doing their work obligation there, so some of the people were mobilised as members of the civilian protection to work for the RAD company.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: If you could be kind enough to just identify some of the workers from the utility company who were collecting the corpses next to the road, as you so testified last week?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: One of the drivers was Milivoje Cvetinovic. Vidak Zivanovic was one of the men who loaded corpses on to the vehicles. There were some other elderly people whom I knew by sight. I didn't know their names. The military department had just mobilised them and sent them over there. In other words, not all of them were the employees of the company where I had worked for a number of years, and whom I knew from -- from that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, also Friday during your direct examination you told us that you were curious and wanted to go towards Konjevic Polje and you took the road there to see what was happening because you had heard certain things were happening there. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Well, at that time did you see any bodies or corpses?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was curious. I didn't have to go there, but I was curious, as men had been sent out to collect corpses along the road to Konjevic Polje, and I had some food in the car and that food, I took to those workers who were engaged in that work and that's when I saw all that.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And this all --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't even know who in Glogova told me that I -- that somebody should go there and collect the bodies, because the bodies kept on coming from Kravica and that's when I went there, I saw the bodies that we went on to collect the following day.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Well, sir, and that's what I want to ask you. You were -- you say here you were curious, you didn't have to go there, "but I was curious as men had been sent out to collect corpses along the road to Konjevic Polje." Then you describe you had some food, et cetera. This, sir, happened -- even according to your most recent version on Friday, this happened before the Kravica incident of July 13th, 1995, did it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, no. This happened on the following day, following the incident in Kravica. It was then when the men collected bodies along the road in the field along the road to Konjevic Polje. This is what I have just explained to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: So your curious -- curiosity trip, when did that happen? Before or after your meeting with Mr. Beara, when you took this trip on the road?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When I saw the killings I went to Kravica and Konjevic Polje and on the following day, when the corpses were being collected, and when the men were sent out to collect the bodies, I took the same road. I went to the same places, to Kravica and Konjevic Polje.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I don't know about your second trip, but we were focusing on your testimony from Friday when you gave evidence during your direct examination, and I asked you during your trip, which was only one at that time, to Konjevic Polje in July of 1995, and that was when you made the trip, and then came back from Konjevic Polje, back to Kravica which you told us you were in your car, we heard that testimony. Thank you for that. I said, "At that time did you see any bodies or corpses, meaning on the -- next to the road or in Konjevic Polje." And your answer on page 81, line 23 through 25, and continuing on page 82, line 1, was as follows: "I was curious. I didn't have to go there. But I was curious, as men had been sent out to collect corpses along the road to Konjevic Polje, and I had some food in the car and that food, I took to those workers who were engaged in that work and that's when I saw all that." Right now, even though you want to talk about Kravica, we're talking specifically about the bodies that you saw on the road from Bratunac to Konjevic Polje, when you took this trip alone out of curiosity. Am I correct, sir, in reading this that, in fact, prior to the Kravica incident, according to your testimony, men had been sent out to collect corpses along the road, and you, in fact, brought them food?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That was on the following day, a day after the incident in Kravica had taken place.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Let me go back then. Did you, sir, prior to viewing the incident at Kravica, did you see any corpses on the road, the Bratunac-Konjevic Polje road?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On the day when I saw the incident in Kravica, I think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Was anyone collecting those corpses along the road at that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: How about the corpses in Konjevic Polje, did you see any at or around the time of the Kravica incident?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. On the following day I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And how about the corpses in Bratunac, sir? Did you see any on or before the Kravica incident that you described?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I believe that this was on the same day, in the evening hours. And the five or six bodies that I saw were collected, according to the driver, there had been even more corpses and that on Thursday -- what am I saying? That on the 14th -- let's say this happened on the 13th, in Kravica, and on the following day all these bodies were taken to Glogova from the schoolyard of the Vuk Karadzic School.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Sir, you said on page 6, lines 15 yesterday -- or Friday, that you heard that some things were happening, "so I went to see, just simply to see what was going on." In connection with that, my question to you is, from whom did you hear that some things were happening. And this -- to put it in proper context for you, I think this was the first trip that you made out of curiosity on the Bratunac-Konjevic Polje road.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You have Kravica and Konjevic Polje in mind, when you asked about the first time I had heard about something having happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. It was probably --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, we were just discussing the schoolyard. And now you're asking me about this, that's why I'm asking you whether you have Konjevic Polje and Kravica in mind or the school.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I have in mind, sir, the first trip you took on the Konjevic Polje-Bratunac road when you became curious, in your testimony last Friday on page 6, you state that that day you heard that some things were happening. All I'm asking you, sir, is from whom did you hear that some things were happened which piqued your curiosity to take a drive all by yourself on the Konjevic Polje-Bratunac road towards Kravica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, rumours, how am I supposed to know who I heard these rumours from?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. Sir, again, I'm going to ask you just to clarify, and thank you for your assistance, your testimony on page 9, line 21 of last Friday. This purported -- sorry, let me just... Okay. Let's talk about the conversation that you had with Mr. Beara supposedly that evening. Am I correct that that was after, it was after you had already met with Mr. Davidovic and Deronjic for drinks and/or dinner, correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, the meeting was after that.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And approximately what time? Sometime after 9.00, you said? 9.00 p.m., correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: After 9.00, 9.00, half past 9.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, when you entered the SDS offices from your office, can you tell us specifically where were the two military policemen stationed?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour. We have been through this. And to go through it back and -- going back forth is -- is confusing and it's unnecessary. We've been through this. He stated who he saw, when he saw them, what was said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: What do you mean by stationed, two military policemen stationed? He's already testified about seeing two military policemen who he doesn't know and doesn't even know -- actually, he excluded that they were from the Bratunac Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Were they in front of the building, were they inside the building. I don't think it's been covered, but if the rule is going to be if we ask the question, they can't --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: What he said is that when he arrived at the building first, there -- obviously, he was stopped by -- I don't remember whether they were military police or not, and then when he went into -- in the room, there were two military police, military police present there. Anyway, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: With all due respect, that wasn't quite --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Sir, where were the two military policemen stationed when you first came to the SDS offices?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were in the office of the SDS secretary.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And you claim Mr. Beara was actually in Mr. Deronjic's office immediately behind that with two other army officers, correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And the four of you, meaning according to your testimony, Mr. Beara, yourself, and these two unknown army officers, were in Mr. Deronjic's office, having this first conversation, correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: This I will not allow, because before you put the question already how many people were there in Deronjic's office, and his answer was categoric, was according to him, Beara, these two officers and himself and no one else. He's already answered that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm accepting it. We were just putting it in context. Fair enough, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Sir, how long did that meeting last with the four of you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: If I had known about this, perhaps I would have measured the time. Half an hour, 40 minutes, how am I to know?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't know in you would like us to break now, given the Court's request earlier today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You have a final question on this that you can put --

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Not one, but I have quite a few.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I imagine so. So let's stop the witness's testimony here. He can be escorted out of the courtroom. Before you leave, sir, I repeat to you that there will be consequences if, between today and tomorrow, you speak or you allow anyone to speak to you on the matters of your testimony. It's an undertaking that you have already made, and which you must stick to. Otherwise, there will be consequences. Yes, usher, you can escort him, please. Where is Ms. Condon?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: She is working in -- at the office at the moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: In the meantime, Ms. Condon is not here, Mr. Sarapa returned during the course of the first session, just for the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You will recall that during the sitting of Tuesday, 20th of March, Ms. Condon, co-counsel in the Defence team for the accused Popovic, made submissions to us, to the Trial Chamber, relating to a news item that appeared on the Tribunal's intranet a few days earlier, namely on the 14th of March, 2007, and which was headed, "ICTY spokesman denounces shameful denial of the Srebrenica genocide." On the occasion other Defence teams voiced their association with Ms. Condon's submissions. As reference was made to the text of the 14th March, 2007, news item by Ms. Condon herself, we will not repeat it. This news item was posted on the ICTY intranet by Mr. Christian-Chartier, and the Trial Chamber has verified that this ICTY intranet news item faithfully reproduces the substance of what Mr. Hodzic is reported as having stated in the course of the ICTY weekly press briefing of the 14th March 2007. The Trial Chamber has also confirmed that Mr. Rafik Hodzic is indeed the spokesman for the Tribunal, excluding the Office of the Prosecutor and acts as the spokesperson for the President and in that capacity for Chambers as well. The substance of Ms. Condon's submission is the following: Firstly, that comment in question, that particular comment in question, is coming from the spokesperson of the very institution where Accused Popovic faces trial. Hence, according to Ms. Condon, it directly impinges on the perception as to whether accused Popovic receives a fair trial. In this context Ms. Condon affirms that her client feels aggrieved. Secondly, that it has clearly emerged in this trial that the accused Popovic's line of Defence would constitute, in the context of Mr. Hodzic's statement, a denial that genocide took place in Srebrenica, something that Mr. Hodzic strongly attacks. Thirdly, that the circumstances of Mr. Hodzic's statement are such as to warrant this Trial Chamber's considering whether to proceed against him pursuant to Rule 77, which provides for or regulates contempt proceedings against persons held to have knowingly and wilfully interfered with the administration of justice. Ms. Condon also informed the Trial Chamber when she raised this issue, that the Accused who are charged with genocide in this case have written a joint letter to the President of this Tribunal. We have carefully considered the submissions advanced by Ms. Condon. We feel that in the circumstances, Ms. Condon and those other Defence teams that associated themselves with her in her submissions did the right thing in raising the matter, bringing it to the attention of the Trial Chamber. The Trial Chamber is of the view that the statements made by Mr. Hodzic were inappropriate, particularly given his role at the Tribunal. The Trial Chamber has no doubt that when Mr. Hodzic makes statements in his capacity as spokesperson of Chambers he has the responsibility to exercise the utmost caution and vigilance in the way he chooses to express himself, especially since his capacity could be interpreted as meaning that he is expressing the views of Chambers and after consultation with same. In this case this Trial Chamber was not consulted by Mr. Hodzic before making his statement, and had we been consulted we would have expressed our concern that nothing is said that could be interpreted adversely in regard to any of the accused in this trial who enjoy the presumption of innocence until proven guilty. Mr. Hodzic's further explanation, albeit belated softens the predicament but in turn highlights the importance of care and vigilance at all times in his statements. Further we intend to convey our concerns in this respect directly to the President of the Tribunal. Without, and to consider the question of the alleged improper inference interference with the administration of justice, particularly in so for as Mr. Hodzic's statement could impinge on the perception of whether the accused Popovic received a fair trial. On in issue the Trial Chamber notes that Mr. Hodzic's statement does not fit in any of the instances giving rise to contempt proceedings listed in subparagraphs (I) to (V) of paragraph A in Rule 77. This list act of contempt, however, is clearly not exhuastive, considering that the same paragraph empowers the Tribunal to hold in contempt those who knowingly and wilfully interfere with its administration of justice, including any person who commits one or more of the acts mentioned in paragraphs (I) to (v) it is obvious therefore that other acts not mongst the ones listed but which in essence amount to an intentional and wilful interference with the Tribunal's administration of justice can be the subject matter of contempt proceedings. It therefore remains to be seen if, by his statement in his capacity as spokesperson of the this Tribunal Mr. Hodzic can be considered to have knowingly and wilfully interfered with administration of justice in the present trial. The Trial Chamber cannot come to the conclusion that Mr. Hodzic's his statement was a deliberate, intentional and wilful attempt to interfere with the proper administration of justice in the present trial. His statement evidently focused on the judgements of the trial and Appeals Chambers in the Krstic case and the fact that the same facts established in this case were endorsed by the International Court of Justice in its recent judgement. It is no surprise to the Trial Chamber that his statement became a source of concern for the accused charged with genocide in this case, especially since they are contesting the charge of genocide, and they too are certainly aware of the judgements in Krstic and that of the international court of justice. But this reason cannot form the basis for considering if the statement by Mr. Hodzic was deliberately intended to undermine these proceedings. The test has to focus on whether it in itself the statement can be construed as a violation of Rule 77. In this context the Trial Chamber does not perceive the statement to have been intended to give the impression that the accused in this trial should think twice before denying that genocide ever took place in Srebrenica or that they stand no chance of being acquitted of the charge of genocide.` In this same context it is significant to note that Mr. Hodzic in another press briefing held on Wednesday, 21st of March, 2007, in reply to a specific question put to him with reference to his previous statement, explained that what he had stated earlier, "Was not in any way a statement on the alleged individual responsibility of any accused whose cases are currently pending before this Tribunal." This and the Trial Chamber's mind is indicative of what I have already pointed out, namely that there is no evidence that Mr. Hodzic's statement was deliberately intended to undermine the administration of justice in this case. In closing, we wish to make it clear that the accused in this case enjoy a presumption of innocence until their guilt or otherwise is finally determined. And their case will be decided on the basis of the evidence which is adduced in this case and not on any previous decision of this Tribunal or any other court on the events that took place in Srebrenica. We stand adjourned until tomorrow. Tomorrow the sitting is in the afternoon. Thank you.
